sections.title: The Prologue
sections.description: The Word became flesh - Jesus' divine origin

sections.title: The Book of Signs
sections.description: Jesus' public ministry with seven signs and great discourses

sections.title: The Book of Glory
sections.description: The upper room, farewell speeches, and Jesus' high priestly prayer

sections.title: Passion and Resurrection
sections.description: Jesus' arrest, crucifixion, resurrection, and appearances

events.title: The Word became flesh
events.description: John's Gospel opens with the magnificent prologue about the Logos - the Word who was with God from the beginning and who himself was God. The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us, full of grace and truth. From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.

events.title: John's testimony and the first disciples
events.description: The Baptist John testifies about Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. Two of John's disciples follow Jesus - Andrew and probably John himself. Andrew brings his brother Simon Peter, and Jesus also calls Philip and Nathanael.

events.title: The Wedding at Cana - Water into Wine
events.description: At a wedding in Cana of Galilee, Jesus performs his first sign by turning water into wine. When the wine runs out, Mary asks Jesus for help. He tells the servants to fill six stone jars with water, and the water becomes the finest wine. This was the beginning of his signs, and his disciples believed in him.

events.title: The Cleansing of the Temple
events.description: Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for the Passover festival and finds the temple filled with money changers and merchants. He makes a whip of cords and drives them all out, overturns the tables of the money changers, and declares that they must not make his Father's house a marketplace.

events.title: The Conversation with Nicodemus
events.description: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and member of the ruling council, comes to Jesus at night. Jesus explains that no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again of water and the Spirit. In this conversation we find the heart of the gospel: "For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life."

events.title: The Woman at the Well in Samaria
events.description: On a journey through Samaria, Jesus stops at Jacob's well and asks a Samaritan woman for water. He reveals that he can give living water that leads to eternal life and shows knowledge of her past. The woman testifies to the whole town, and many Samaritans come to believe in Jesus as the Savior of the world.

events.title: The Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
events.description: At the Pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, Jesus heals a man who has been ill for thirty-eight years. Jesus says to him: "Get up, pick up your mat and walk!" Because this happens on the Sabbath, the Jewish leaders begin to persecute Jesus. He defends himself by saying that his Father is still working, and so is he.

events.title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
events.description: A large crowd follows Jesus to the other side of the Sea of Galilee. With only five barley loaves and two fish from a boy, Jesus feeds more than five thousand people, and twelve baskets of bread are left over. This is the fourth sign, and the people want to make him king.

events.title: Jesus Walks on Water
events.description: In the evening, the disciples go out onto the sea in a boat while Jesus withdraws alone to the mountain. When the wind rises and the waves grow large, they see Jesus walking toward them on the water. He says: "It is I. Do not be afraid!" The boat immediately reaches land.

events.title: The Bread of Life Discourse
events.description: In the synagogue in Capernaum, Jesus delivers the profound sermon on the bread of life. He declares: "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty." Many of his disciples leave him after this sermon, but Peter confesses: "Lord, whom shall we go to? You have the words of eternal life."

events.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
events.description: The scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery before Jesus to test him. Jesus bends down and writes on the ground, saying: "Let any one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her." One by one they leave, and Jesus says to the woman: "Neither do I condemn you. Go now and leave your life of sin."

events.title: "I Am the Light of the World"
events.description: During the Feast of Tabernacles in Jerusalem, Jesus declares: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life." The Pharisees challenge him, but Jesus testifies to his relationship with the Father and says: "Before Abraham was born, I am." They pick up stones to throw at him.

events.title: The Healing of the Man Born Blind
events.description: Jesus heals a man who had been blind from birth by making mud with saliva, applying it to the man's eyes, and sending him to the Pool of Siloam to wash. The Pharisees interrogate the healed man repeatedly and cast him out of the synagogue. Jesus finds him, reveals himself as the Son of Man, and the man worships him.

events.title: The Good Shepherd Discourse
events.description: Jesus uses the image of the shepherd and the flock to describe his relationship with his own. He declares: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." He also speaks of having other sheep that are not of this fold, and that he has authority to lay down his life and take it up again.

events.title: The Raising of Lazarus
events.description: Jesus' friend Lazarus in Bethany falls ill and dies. Jesus waits two days before going there, by which time Lazarus has been in the tomb for four days. Martha confesses her faith, and Jesus declares: "I am the resurrection and the life." At the tomb, Jesus weeps, prays to the Father, and calls out: "Lazarus, come out!" The dead man comes out, bound with burial cloths. This final and greatest sign leads the council to decide to kill Jesus.

events.title: Mary Anoints Jesus in Bethany
events.description: Six days before Passover, they hold a meal for Jesus in Bethany. Mary takes an alabaster jar of expensive nard ointment and anoints Jesus' feet, wiping them with her hair. Judas Iscariot protests against the waste, but Jesus says she has kept it for his burial.

events.title: The Entry into Jerusalem
events.description: The day after the anointing in Bethany, Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a young donkey while the crowd waves palm branches and shouts, "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!" The Pharisees say to one another, "The whole world has gone after him."

events.title: The Foot Washing
events.description: During the last meal, Jesus rises, takes off his outer garment, wraps a towel around his waist, and begins to wash the disciples' feet. Peter protests at first, but Jesus explains that this is an example of service. He gives them a new command: "Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another."

events.title: The Farewell Discourses and the Promise of the Advocate
events.description: Jesus comforts his disciples with the words, "In my Father's house there are many rooms." He promises them another Advocate, the Holy Spirit, who will be with them forever. He uses the image of the vine and the branches to describe their unity with him and warns that the world will hate them. He promises that the Spirit will guide them into all truth.

events.title: Jesus' High Priestly Prayer
events.description: Jesus looks up to heaven and prays his great intercessory prayer. First, he prays for himself to be glorified, then for his disciples, asking that the Father keep them in his name and sanctify them in the truth. Finally, he prays for all who will believe through their message, that they may all be one.

events.title: The Arrest in the Garden
events.description: Jesus goes with his disciples across the Kidron Valley to a garden where Judas arrives with a detachment of soldiers and guards from the chief priests. When Jesus says, "I am he," they fall to the ground. Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant Malchus, but Jesus tells him to put his sword back in its sheath.

events.title: Peter's Denial and the Trial before Pilate
events.description: While Jesus is questioned by the high priest Annas and then Caiaphas, Peter denies knowing Jesus three times. Jesus is brought to Pilate, who finds him innocent but yields to the crowd's demands. Pilate asks, "What is truth?" and tries to release him, but the people choose Barabbas.

events.title: The Crucifixion and Death of Jesus
events.description: Jesus carries his own cross to Golgotha where he is crucified between two others. Pilate places a sign on the cross reading, "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews." At the foot of the cross stand his mother, and Jesus entrusts her to the disciple whom he loved. He says, "It is finished," bows his head, and gives up his spirit. A soldier pierces his side with a spear.

events.title: The Empty Tomb and Mary Magdalene
events.description: Early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb and finds the stone rolled away. Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved run to the tomb and find it empty. Mary stands weeping outside the tomb. Jesus appears to her, and she recognizes him when he says her name. He sends her to the disciples with the message: "I am ascending to my Father."

events.title: Jesus Appears to the Disciples and Thomas
events.description: On the evening of Resurrection Day, Jesus appears to the disciples behind locked doors, shows them his hands and his side, and breathes on them: "Receive the Holy Spirit." Thomas is not present and refuses to believe. Eight days later, Jesus appears again, and Thomas confesses: "My Lord and my God!" Jesus says: "Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed."

events.title: The Great Catch of Fish and the Restoration of Peter
events.description: By the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus appears to seven disciples who had fished all night without catching anything. He tells them to cast the net on the right side, and they catch 153 large fish. During a meal on the shore, Jesus asks Peter three times: "Do you love me?" and gives him the commission: "Feed my sheep." In this way, Jesus restores Peter after his three denials.
